findings.title: Single MetricsMiddleware instance has its `next` field overwritten on every request (data race)
findings.body:
`NewMetricsMiddleware` creates one `*MetricsMiddleware` up front. The returned `ClientMiddlewareFunc` then sets `imw.next = next` and returns that same shared instance.

`client.Decorator` rebuilds the middleware chain on every QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth and CollectMetrics call through `clientFromMiddlewares`. So concurrent plugin requests write `imw.next` at the same time other goroutines read it via `m.next.QueryData(...)` and similar calls. That is a data race the race detector will flag, and request A may end up running request B's downstream chain.

This pattern was carried over unchanged from `NewInstrumentationMiddleware`. Since this code is being reworked anyway, the middleware should return a fresh struct per call instead, e.g. `&MetricsMiddleware{pluginMetrics: imw.pluginMetrics, pluginRegistry: imw.pluginRegistry, next: next}`.

findings.title: LoggerMiddleware now silently depends on ContextualLoggerMiddleware running before it
findings.body:
`logRequest` used to add `pluginId`, `endpoint`, `uname`, `dsName`, `dsUID` and `traceID` to the "Plugin Request Completed" (`grafana-data-egress`) log line itself. It now relies entirely on `m.logger.FromContext(ctx)` and on attributes that `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` placed in the context earlier in the chain.

If `NewLoggerMiddleware` is used without `NewContextualLoggerMiddleware` ahead of it, those identifying fields disappear from the egress log with no error. That includes tests, enterprise or other compositions, and any future reordering of `CreateMiddlewares`.

The old doc note saying the instrumentation middleware must sit at the top of the stack was removed, and no replacement documents the new ordering requirement. Either document the requirement on `NewLoggerMiddleware`/`CreateMiddlewares`, or keep the explicit fields in the logger middleware.

findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a new empty logger, so logged calls cannot be asserted
findings.body:
`TestLogger.FromContext` returns `NewTestLogger()`, a fresh instance, not the receiver. `LoggerMiddleware` now always logs through `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`.

A test that injects a `TestLogger` and checks `InfoLogs.Calls`, `Message` or `Ctx` will therefore always see zero calls. The fake cannot be used to verify the middleware's logging. Returning `f`, or a logger that shares the recorded state, would make the fake usable for this purpose.

findings.title: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware and changed log composition are untested
findings.body:
The PR adds a new middleware and moves the source of the egress log's identifying fields (pluginId, endpoint, uname, dsName, dsUID, traceID) from explicit parameters to context-derived attributes.

No test checks either of these:
- that `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` attaches the expected attributes for each endpoint;
- that the "Plugin Request Completed" log still carries them when the middlewares are chained in production order.

A regression here, such as a reordering or a missing attribute, would silently degrade the data-egress logs.
